2022, the deficit had decreased to 5.4 percent of GDP, reflecting the phasing out of pandemic-
related aid and recovery in the economy more broadly. 
For FY 2023, the deficit increased $320 billion to $1.70 trillion, equal to 6.3 percent of GDP, as 
lower receipts outweighed decreased spending.  Receipts shrank by $457 billion from FY 2022 
to FY 2023.  The decrease was related to more normal capital gains realizations in 2022—taxes 
of which are paid in FY 2023—whereas historically high realizations in 2021 had boosted 
receipts in FY 2022.  Outlays decreased by $137 billion in FY 2023, partly reflecting the impact 
of Biden v. Nebraska on certain student loan relief programs.  However, the decrease in the 
Department of Education’s net outlays was offset by higher outlays for national defense, Social 
Security, Medicare, and net interest.   
At the end of FY 2023, gross federal debt stood at 122.9 percent of GDP ($33.2 trillion), up from 
122.2 percent of GDP ($30.9 trillion) at the end of fiscal year 2022.  Debt held by the public was 
$2632 trillion (97.6 percent of GDP) at the end of FY 2023, up from $24.3 trillion by the end of 
fiscal year 2022 (96.0 percent of GDP).  In June 2023, the Treasury’s borrowing limit was 
suspended until 2025.
